originality.rationale: Trudgian section 4 asks the equality infinitude question but gives no infinite dyadic-exponent classification. A very close prior published result exhausts two-prime singleton-cofactor layers a=2..49, covering all dyadic exponents through 32, which are credited rather than claimed as novel. Its finite theorem has no statement for a>=50; the current proof establishes all t>=6 (a>=64) uniformly. OEIS supplies example values only; targeted published-finding corpus/literature checks found no implication covering the infinite result. Residual possibility of unlocated equivalent literature is explicit.
residual_risks: An unlocated general congruence or divisibility theorem could imply dyadic nonexistence.
The published a<=49 theorem overlaps t<=5 completely; only the unbounded higher-exponent range constitutes incremental coverage.
